text: Spotlight: DEEPAKFERT.NS, 30.9 years of history, 5y CAGR 32.4%, worst drawdown -86.2%, -16.4% from its all-time high.

speaker: Kimi K3
text: Deepak Fertilizers is the kind of compounder that can get you to 10x if you survive the drawdowns — 32% five-year CAGR is real, but that -86% max drawdown means you'd have needed diamond hands in 2020. The latest quarter shows operating margins expanding to 19.4% from 8.3% just two quarters ago, and the 12.6% earnings surprise with a 7.5% next-day pop suggests the street is still underestimating the structural shift toward specialty chemicals. At 1.38 beta and only 0.42 correlation to Nifty, this moves to its own beat — good for diversification, bad for sleep. For your Rs 10k, the 0.38% round-trip delivery cost on Zerodha is trivial, but the 20% short-term tax on gains under 12 months bites; hold past a year and it drops to 12.5% with the first Rs 1.25L exempt. On the US side, NVDA at $125 with RSI 15 is oversold on the daily, but the -23% five-day drop with 2.18x volume says institutions are still exiting — fractional shares let you dollar-cost in, but don't kid yourself that $100 becomes $1,000 in a year at 25% CAGR. That's a 4-year journey at best.

speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: Hind Copper's 96.8% max drawdown is a portfolio killer — you'd need a 2,400% rally just to recover from the lows, and insiders have sold ₹33 crore in the last six months with zero buys. That 29.6% five-year CAGR looks great on paper but it's built on a commodity cycle that's already rolling over, with the stock 44.6% off its high and down 18.7% this calendar year. For your ₹10k, the 0.38% round-trip cost on Zerodha delivery is trivial, but the 20% short-term tax bites hard if you're wrong on timing; at 1.58 beta to Nifty, this thing amplifies every market wobble. On the US side, NVDA at RSI 15 with 2.18x volume isn't a buy signal — it's a falling knife with institutions still heading for the exits, and your $100 fractional position won't dodge the drawdown.
